title: Country Boundary Downloader: Full Outlines
description: Download a country's complete boundary — every polygon part, islands included — with the Country Boundary Downloader, as KML or GeoJSON. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, France arrives as a MultiPolygon: the mainland plus Corsica and its coastal islands in a single file, with the enclosed land area computed from the outline.
quick_answer: The Country Boundary Downloader gives you a country's complete boundary as one file — all polygon parts, islands included — in KML or GeoJSON. Pick the country and download the outline with its land area computed from the geometry — raw material for maps that need real borders.

body.t: A true national outline beats a traced approximation in every classroom and report. Style it, label it, print it — the geometry is the real shape.
Clip global datasets to one country, or mask everything outside it. The boundary file is the cookie cutter; your data is the dough.

covers the cities and counties below this level.
The computed enclosed area lets you sanity-check published country areas — outline-derived figures and almanac figures should broadly agree, and the differences are instructive.
Indonesia and the Philippines download as thousands of island polygons in one MultiPolygon — ‘complete’ means every part, which is why these files are big and why partial ones mislead.
France’s file pairs the European mainland polygon with Corsica; Greece adds its island constellation. One feature, many parts — GIS software handles the family as a single country.

popular_table.note: Boundaries reflect OpenStreetMap’s documented positions, including its handling of disputed areas. Almanac land areas may differ slightly — outlines include coastal detail and tidal choices that statistics smooth away.

faq: Every country present in the open boundary data — effectively the whole world map, from France to Fiji. A place without a recorded administrative outline is the rare exception.

The download follows the boundary record for the country as mapped — metropolitan outlines and separately-administered territories are distinct entries in the data. Download the territory itself when you need it.
KML for Google Earth and sharing; GeoJSON for GIS, web maps and code. Same outline in both — choose by destination, not by data.
Why is the file so large?
Coastlines are fractal in spirit: detailed countries carry hundreds of thousands of outline points. Size is fidelity. Simplify in your GIS if your use allows it.
Can I get just one island or region?
Use the Boundary KML Downloader for sub-national outlines — provinces, states and islands with their own administrative records live there.
Yes — Lesotho inside South Africa, and similar geometries, arrive as their own complete country files; the surrounding country’s outline has the hole where the enclave sits.
OpenStreetMap’s documented position, as with all boundary data here. The file is a working geometry, not a diplomatic ruling.
